subject: physics_2
question_text: Obtain an expression for the mutual inductance (M) of two long coaxially placed solenoids.

mark_split.label: Setup and the field of S₁

verification.note: The 1+1+1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. For this Physics-II paper the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers. Physics hand-checked: B₁ = μ₀N₁i₁/l inside S₁; flux linkage of S₂ = N₂B₁A; M₂₁ = N₂Φ₂/i₁ = μ₀N₁N₂A/l; the reverse case gives M₁₂ = the same expression, so M = μ₀N₁N₂A/l = μ₀n₁n₂Al with n = N/l — symbols stated on the card. NOTE: this derivation is a Long Answer in most other syllabuses; this book prints it as a 4-mark SAQ and the card keeps the book's section. The figure cannot rely on occlusion (outline-only renderer), so the outer solenoid is drawn as two long rails with the inner pair of rails clearly between them on one dashed axis.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.label: Figure: two coaxial solenoids
steps.margin_note: Draw the outer solenoid as two long rails and the inner one clearly between them, both on one dashed axis. Mark the common length l.
steps.why: The whole derivation lives on this geometry: same length, same axis, one solenoid wound over the other, so the inner field passes through every turn of the outer coil.
common_mistakes: Drawing two separate coils side by side. The solenoids share one axis, one inside the other.

recall.must_convey: That a figure of two coaxial solenoids on one axis is drawn, inner S₁ and outer S₂, with the common length l marked.
reject: mu nought N1 N2 A by l

steps.memory_tip: One axis, two solenoids: draw the long outer rails first, then the shorter pair of rails inside.

steps.margin_note: First mark. Declare every symbol once — l, A, N₁, N₂, i₁ — before any formula uses it.
steps.why: Every later line reuses these symbols, so declaring them once — length, area, turns, current — is what makes the derivation readable and markable. A is the cross-sectional area of the INNER solenoid. Two coaxial solenoids cannot share an area, and it is the inner one that matters both ways: the inner solenoid's field exists only over its own area, and the outer solenoid's uniform field crosses the inner coil over that same area.
common_mistakes: Writing B = μ₀ni with n undefined. Say which count you use: here N₁ is the TOTAL number of turns, so B₁ = μ₀N₁i₁/l.

recall.must_convey: That two coaxial solenoids of equal length and area are set up, and the field of the inner one is μ₀N₁i₁/l.
accept: B1 equals mu nought N1 i1 by l

steps.memory_tip: Same l, same A, turns N₁ and N₂ — set the stage in one sentence before any formula.

steps.why: Mutual inductance is defined through the flux LINKAGE of the second coil, so counting all N₂ turns is the step that matters.
common_mistakes: Using the flux through one turn only. The linkage multiplies by all N₂ turns.

steps.why: The definition M = flux linkage over current turns the geometry into a single constant; i₁ cancels, so M depends only on the coils, not on the current.
common_mistakes: Leaving i₁ in the final expression. The current cancels — inductance depends only on geometry and medium.

steps.margin_note: Fourth mark. Show both directions agree, then box M in either form — total turns or turns per unit length.
steps.why: Running the argument both ways shows M₁₂ = M₂₁ — one mutual inductance for the pair, whichever coil carries the current. That symmetry is the point of the word mutual.
common_mistakes: Stopping after M₂₁. The question asks for the mutual inductance of the pair, so show that both directions agree.
